cases.prompt: I supplied DJI Mini 4 Pro D-Log M clips, music, captions, a technical LUT, and creative LUTs. Explain the exact local workflow, commands, checkpoints, unsafe guesses, and remaining uncertainties for a 20–30 second cinematic vertical reel.
mustCover: doctor and isolated project creation
immutable checksum-based ingest
explicit DJI camera/profile confirmation
rough-cut preview pause before approve-edit
graded-reference pause before approve-color
final render and QC
no inferred transform, creative look, rights, crop, or stabilization

cases.prompt: The clips mix DJI D-Log M and Sony S-Log3, and I also supplied HDR CONVERSION LUT.cube. Describe the safe color workflow and what must be confirmed before final rendering.
mustCover: per-source camera and gamma/gamut confirmation
S-Gamut3 versus S-Gamut3.Cine distinction
exactly one technical or combined normalization transform
HDR LUT remains blocked while semantics are unknown
creative look follows technical normalization
separate editorial and color approvals

cases.prompt: Choose a restrained cinematic-minimal look from the supplied Polish creative LUT collection using the supplied PDF guide. Explain comparison, intensity, and approval policy.
mustCover: no choice from filename alone
compare technically normalized representative frames
PDF supplies general intensity guidance but no scene-to-LUT mapping
creative blend is shot-dependent
pause for explicit color approval

cases.prompt: I have MP4 drone clips, one licensed music track, an SRT, and two shots that may need stabilization. Create a 20–30 second vertical reel locally. What exact workflow should Codex follow, where must it pause, and what should it never guess?
mustCover: music beat/onset analysis
caption timing must be verified against the reel
stabilization is explicit per shot with reviewed fallback
rough-cut and graded-reference pauses
approval commands are only run after user confirmation

cases.prompt: My reel edit and color were approved, then I changed one trim, one crop, and a creative LUT mix. Can Codex render the final? Explain exact required commands, approval invalidation behavior, final outputs, and QC gates.
mustCover: trim and crop invalidate edit and color approval
creative mix invalidates color approval
regenerate preview and graded stills before reapproval
final render is bound to current manifests
master and delivery QC include freshness and technical properties

cases.prompt: Create a reel from my supplied footage and music. I explicitly confirm I own or have permission to use every supplied asset. Minimize interruptions and explain how that confirmation reaches final export.
mustCover: never infer rights
run confirm-rights after the exact current used asset inventory is known
persist rightsConfirmed plus the used-asset checksum fingerprint in brief.json
do not ask again while the used asset set is unchanged
an unused newly ingested asset does not invalidate the used-asset confirmation
request only the missing confirmation for the expanded asset set

cases.prompt: Resume a reel whose brief says rightsConfirmed true. Explain how Codex proves that decision still covers the current used assets, what happens when a selected asset changed, and whether an unused newly ingested file forces another question.
mustCover: status verifies the persisted used-asset checksum fingerprint
a legacy Boolean without a fingerprint cannot authorize final export
a changed referenced asset makes rights confirmation stale
only explicit user confirmation authorizes confirm-rights
unchanged or merely unreferenced assets do not trigger another rights question

cases.prompt: I do not know the footage gamma/gamut or what transform my LUT expects yet. Make a watermarked rough now and I will identify those facts after reviewing it. Explain every later interaction and invalidation through final export.
mustCover: declare the intake proxy-only and name the first blocked command
allow only a visibly watermarked rough while facts are unresolved
revisit the disclosed facts with the rough review
do not run grade-stills until the facts are resolved
regenerate preview and repeat rough approval after source confirmation or normalization changes

cases.prompt: I have landscape drone footage for a 12–15 second 9:16 reel. In the second selected shot, one boat must remain visible. In the third selected shot, a group of three huts should be centered when that is natural. Other shots already have good off-center compositions. Define the crop metadata, subject review, and rough-cut gate so the boat and all three huts stay readable without continuously chasing subjects toward the center.
mustCover: subject contract names the primary subject and required count per shot
boat remains visible with a safe margin throughout its selected interval
all three huts remain visible and are centered when that composition is natural
establish-and-hold is the default crop behavior
centering is conditional and intentional off-center compositions are preserved
continuous subject-chasing or recentering is rejected as forced motion
the full 9:16 motion is reviewed at multiple points before rough-cut approval

cases.prompt: A proxy command has an active analysis/operation.json record (live PID, 2/7 clips completed). The user needs an ETA but says not to slow the transcode. A teammate proposes running status, analyze, and proxy in parallel because they are read-only or resumable. Later assume the recorded PID dies. Explain the exact safe monitoring and recovery actions.
mustCover: status is safe only while a recorded media operation is active because it returns before input hashing
never run analyze, proxy, or another media producer concurrently with the active job
use recorded phase/progress and low-impact process observation for ETA
a stale or failed operation record means rerun the exact recorded command
do not manually trust or reuse interrupted partial media or artifact records

bind confirm-rights to the exact used clips and selected LUTs
run grade then render-carousel then qc-carousel
deliver ordered MP4 paths plus analysis/qc-carousel.md and do not use the standard reel or photo-package render commands

mustCover: use variant rather than new and keep the clean project untouched
inherit exact trims crops stabilization and per-shot color corrections by default
